stories.new_fact: The Supreme Court's new term begins October 5 with climate, immigration, voting, gun-rights and religious-rights cases on the agenda.
stories.new_takeaway: The court term is best understood as a cost-allocation and compliance calendar for cities, energy firms, states, schools and election offices.
stories.why_now: The term begins today and the first climate case starts the operational watch.
stories.previous_coverage: No full segment in the previous seven episodes; no repeated conclusion.
stories.uncertainty: Case outcomes, opinion timing and final scope are unknown.
stories.watch: Watch for early signals on whether climate-liability suits can proceed and for December arguments on Arizona voting rules.

stories.new_fact: The U.S. military said it struck another suspected drug-smuggling boat Sunday, killing four people, bringing AP's reported campaign total to at least 235 killed in 70 strikes.
stories.new_takeaway: The operational question is whether evidence and legal authority keep pace as the campaign expands.
stories.why_now: The strike occurred Sunday and AP published details overnight.
stories.previous_coverage: No full segment in the prior seven episodes.
stories.uncertainty: The military did not provide public evidence that the vessel carried drugs; legal challenges or congressional oversight may change the path.
stories.watch: Watch for congressional, court or partner-government demands for evidence or limits before land operations expand.

stories.new_fact: Columbus City Council has Ordinance 2313-2026 on the October 5 agenda for a Danbert construction contract of up to $12,600,862.73 plus $2,000 in prevailing-wage services.
stories.new_takeaway: The project combines stormwater adaptation, permeable pavement, waterline relocation and street restoration, so residents should judge both drainage and construction recovery.
stories.why_now: The item is on tonight's council agenda and minutes are not final.
stories.previous_coverage: No prior seven-episode coverage of this project.
stories.uncertainty: Council action, Ohio Water Development Authority loan approval, notice-to-proceed date and final construction staging remain pending.
stories.watch: Watch council action and the notice-to-proceed date that starts the 630-day completion window.

stories.new_fact: Fannie Mae aligned credit-score LLPAs across Classic FICO and VantageScore 4.0, applying to whole loans purchased on or after October 1 and MBS deliveries with issue dates on or after October 1.
stories.new_takeaway: The operational issue is pricing-engine, lock-desk, secondary-marketing and QC consistency, not a generic rate recap and not the same as bi-merge credit reporting.
stories.why_now: The effective date is current for this week's locks and delivery work.
stories.previous_coverage: Recent episodes covered possible bi-merge and score-model implementation, but not this effective Fannie pricing alignment as the lead.
stories.uncertainty: Lenders still need investor acceptance, system readiness and pricing-table validation.
stories.watch: Watch for lender or investor exceptions, incorrect LLPA treatment, and borrower quote changes tied to score-model choice.
stories.date_exception: Specialist beat used one explicitly dated operational update from the last seven days because Monday mortgage policy news was otherwise quiet and the effective date changes current pricing work.

stories.new_fact: Mastercard said it is working with Skyfire on Know Your Agent technology to help financial institutions and merchants recognize trusted AI agents across the ecosystem.
stories.new_takeaway: Agent payments shift the bank AI question toward authorization context, dispute design and customer intent at transaction time.
stories.why_now: The update is a previously uncovered specialist development from the last week and changes the bank AI ledger.
stories.previous_coverage: Recent episodes covered Zopa, Bank of America, Barclays and Kyndryl/BIL; no prior full segment on Mastercard KYA risk tools.
stories.uncertainty: No live approval volume, fraud-rate movement, false-positive rate or dispute baseline was disclosed.
stories.watch: Watch for issuer live-volume, fraud-loss, approval-rate or dispute-process evidence.
stories.ledger_row_changed: Mastercard / Skyfire, consumer payments and compliance control; new announced row added for Know Your Agent authorization context.
stories.date_exception: Specialist beat used one explicitly dated update from the last seven days because no higher-evidence bank AI production metric emerged within 48 hours.

stories.new_fact: President Trump named National Intelligence Director Jay Clayton to lead a new federal AI task force reporting to Trump and his chief of staff.
stories.new_takeaway: The task force matters only if it turns voluntary AI oversight into dates, standards, reporting duties or procurement consequences.
stories.why_now: The appointment was announced Sunday and AP published the new federal structure.
stories.previous_coverage: Recent episodes covered agent probing and OpenAI safety pauses; this is a distinct federal policy channel.
stories.uncertainty: No binding rules, technical measurements or evaluation standards were announced.
stories.watch: Watch for published standards, reporting duties, procurement conditions or agency guidance that binds frontier labs or buyers.
stories.frontier_bar: Policy that may bind labs directly; no capability or benchmark claim.

stories.new_fact: Asian equities rose after weak U.S. jobs data while investors looked ahead to 10-year and 30-year Treasury auctions and oil remained elevated.
stories.new_takeaway: Borrowing-cost relief requires Treasury demand and calmer oil, not just a better equity tape.
stories.why_now: Monday market setup frames mortgage and municipal finance decisions for the week.
stories.previous_coverage: Recent episodes covered jobs-report relief and yield pressure; this was kept compact to avoid repetition.
stories.uncertainty: Auction demand, oil moves and Fed minutes could change the rate signal.
stories.watch: Watch this week's Treasury auctions and Wednesday Fed minutes.

stories.new_fact: NWS showed no Franklin County alerts over the next five days and forecast a dry Monday near 70 with a cool night.
stories.new_takeaway: Weather should not disrupt commute, school, jobsite or errand plans today.
stories.previous_coverage: Routine weather appears daily; no repeated phrasing was reused.
stories.uncertainty: Later-week cold-front timing and shower coverage can change.
stories.watch: Watch Friday's possible cold front and showers.
